description: Twelve independently generated composed Philadelphia exterior stills. Not in-app screenshots, not surveyed replicas.
commonPrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept, photoreal architectural visualization. Asset: one individual ultra-detailed premium Philadelphia exterior concept still for the existing Octoberline typewriter studio window. EXTERIOR ONLY: no window frame, no interior, no typewriter, no UI, no labels or collage. Wide cinematic landscape 16:9, highest available detail, refined realistic architectural photography and physically based archviz, not a game screenshot or low-poly render. This is a composed Philadelphia architectural view, not a survey photograph.
Architectural fidelity: recognizable actual Philadelphia buildings, not a generic American skyline. PECO headquarters is a nearer, modest-height shallow rectangular slab of shiny black glass with fine dark panel joints, a visible narrow side return and a wraparound LED crown reading exactly "PECO" in warm white pixels. Keep crown clear and legible; do not make PECO a supertall. Behind it, selectively use One Liberty Place (slender blue glass, intricate layered stepped angular crown, long silver spire) and Two Liberty Place (lower and broader, a related but different compact stepped crown); Comcast Technology Center (tallest, distinctly stepped industrial silver/glass mass with visible structural spine and long OFFSET illuminated blade); Comcast Center (shorter tapered FACETED silvery glass obelisk, transparent recessed crown, clearly different outline). BNY Mellon has a broad pyramidal roof; Three Logan Square adds warm rose granite, deep windows and sculpted setbacks. Buildings must show actual thickness, two differently lit facades, fine curtain-wall mullions, glass reflections, recessed floors, correct crown complexity, no repeated tower primitives. No identical rectangular twin skyscrapers, no World Trade Center forms, no Empire State/Chrysler/NYC landmarks, no invented sci-fi architecture.
Image quality: rich restrained color, ray-traced soft shadow feel, crisp stone and brick joints, believable restrained wear, deep window recesses, fully dimensional layered urban blocks. Architectural details stay sharp rather than painterly noise. Real mature autumn trees with branched structure and individual leaves; enough openings that skyline crowns remain unobstructed. No block cars, no cars at all; quiet human-scale street or roofscape life is optional and tiny. No text except PECO building crown. Ground/near roofs lower 25-35%, buildings center 45-55%, modest breathing sky above. Avoid fisheye, extreme wide distortion, flat painted silhouettes, exaggerated bloom, oversaturation, uniform window checkerboards.
Further fidelity constraints: BNY Mellon Center is primarily a glass-and-metal shaft with vertical articulation and a stainless-toned broad pyramidal roof, NOT a solid ornate stone skyscraper. Avoid Manhattan Art Deco inventions. Townhouse brick/brownstone/blue-marble fronts should feel authentically Philadelphia, not a uniform Parisian limestone boulevard. These concepts can recompose geography but should honor each landmark's recognizable architectural identity.

variants.title: Rittenhouse, late October
variants.scene: Signature balanced composition: elevated third-to-fourth-floor sightline over a richly detailed Rittenhouse/Delancey-inspired foreground. Lower left and right contain a few elegant attached Philadelphia brownstone and Pennsylvania blue-marble townhouses with projecting semi-hexagonal bays, carved lintels, slate mansards, cross-braced dormers and iron railings. Autumn plane-tree canopy frames lower edges but opens in the middle. PECO sits unobscured mid-left; unequal Liberty towers and the two DIFFERENT Comcast towers form a staggered full Center City skyline behind, with several handsome intermediate buildings. Golden late afternoon, burnished copper leaves, cool blue reflective glass, subtle rose sky. Most inviting premium option, architectural realism with deep perspective.
